newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares close up on earnings hopes.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares close up on earnings hopes.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices reversed slight early losses on Friday, to finish higher as investors built positions in counters that were expected to post solid earnings for 1996, brokers said.
The B share index inched up 0.19 points or 0.13 percent to close at 149.05 on turnover of HK$90.82 million compared with Thursday's HK$107.54 million.
The A share index rose 2.29 points or 0.63 percent to end at 364.69 points on turnover of 7.05 billion yuan, against 8.05 billion yuan in the previous session.
Investors were reducing exposure to firms likely to report disappointing 1996 results and diverting funds to those with good earnings outlooks, brokers said.
"Despite the B share rise, foreign institutional selling was seen increasing on Friday," said a broker with China Southern Securities Co Ltd.
"Maybe foreign institutions feel safer to have more cash in their hands ahead of the two-week Chinese lunar new year holiday which starts on February 3," the broker said.
B shares will continue to move in line with the A share market, brokers said.
On the B share market, beverage maker Shenbao performed strongest and surged HK$0.35 or 6.54 percent to HK$5.70 on trade of 390,510 shares.

Property issue Hainan Pearl River was the most active counter on volume of 1.65 million shares, rising HK$0.07 to HK$3.31, lifted by investor optimism over the firm's unreleased 1996 results, brokers said.
Guangdong Expressway, the third biggest gainer, advanced HK$0.16 or 2.15 percent to HK$7.59, with 227,900 shares traded.

On the A share market, Datong Cement Co Ltd, which listed 13.50 million A shares in Shenzhen on Friday, closed at 16.06 yuan in trade of 11.22 million shares compared with a recent offer price of 7.15 yuan.
Hotelier Dalian Friendship (Group) Co Ltd, which floated 35 million A shares in Shenzhen on Friday, ended the session at 16.93 yuan. The shares were issued at 9.80 yuan each earlier this month.
Profit-taking sent Shenzhen Fangda, a building materials producer, down 0.61 yuan or 3.48 percent to 16.90 yuan, brokers said.
